spans.title: No Hereditary Scratcher
spans.blurb: A boy dining before a solemn court is seized by an itch, and nothing in English history offers guidance on what to do next.

spans.title: Rags and Splendours
spans.blurb: A little prince and a beggar boy trade stories of their worlds, then trade clothes for a lark, and a mirror shows them something strange.

books.pairNote: One stages the clothes swap, the other plays out a comic consequence at court; they complement without repeating.

spans.title: Go Back to Lenox
spans.blurb: An old man arrives at a hotel trailing his vanished wife and finds a letter already waiting, four words scrawled in a peculiar shade of yellow pencil.

spans.title: Dear Madman
spans.blurb: A gentleman of independent means picks his professions, and his railway stops, purely on whim. His latest stop lands him at a friend's door at exactly the wrong moment.

spans.title: Six Red Flags
spans.blurb: The hillside slides down onto the railway line, and three children with seven minutes and nothing red must find a way to warn the 11.29.
spans.brokenNote: The final sentence is cut off in the middle of its phrase, ending on 'the sticks of the little red', a visible truncation right at the emotional climax.

spans.title: The Trophy Hat
spans.blurb: A freckled schoolgirl bursts in waving a gentleman's hat found where the enemy airship passed over, and she is not about to surrender it to anyone.

spans.title: A Letter of Introduction
spans.blurb: A muddy stranger climbs through a lady's library window, apologizes beautifully, blocks her way to the bell, and seems to know exactly who everyone is.

books.pairNote: The hat found in one is the hat lost in the other; the link enriches both rather than repeating a payoff.

spans.title: A Yellow Smell
spans.blurb: In a damp week the smell arrives, creeping through every room of the house, hanging over her bed at night. She cannot name it, but she keeps trying.
spans.spoilerNote: The rubbed streak round the room quietly foreshadows the tale's closing revelation without explaining it.

spans.title: The Woman Behind the Pattern
spans.blurb: By moonlight the wallpaper pattern shakes. She begs her doctor husband to take her away; he knows better, of course. So she keeps watching.
spans.spoilerNote: Reveals the woman behind the pattern, a development the full tale builds to gradually, though the ending stays hidden.

spans.title: A Voice in the Dark
spans.blurb: An officers' mess drowses through a hot evening of engagement talk until a tired voice lifts out of the darkness, asking for her husband.

spans.title: The Immortal Druggist
spans.blurb: On a wet London Sunday a man steps into a chemist's shop and comes to believe the dull fellow behind the counter is no mortal at all.

spans.title: The Pensive Citadel
spans.blurb: At half past three on a July morning a schoolboy rises to run away, pausing to kiss a picture goodbye and smuggle a mighty trunk past his headmaster's door.

spans.title: The Trick With the Old Hat
spans.blurb: A schoolboy learns from an older boy that a certain old hat, moved just so, buys cakes for free in any shop in town.

spans.title: The Brother's Watch
spans.blurb: To puncture his friend's dogmatic streak, a doctor hands over a newly cleaned pocket watch and asks what can possibly be read from it.
